subject: Civil Engineering
title: What Is a Structural Load?
description: Learn What Is a Structural Load? in one minute.

hook.text: Every building fights gravity every second of every day. The fight never stops.

buildup.text: Dead loads are the weight of the building itself — walls, floors, and the roof.

discovery.text: Live loads are everything that moves — people, furniture, snow, and wind.

twist.text: Engineers must design for loads that haven't happened yet, including rare extremes.

climax.text: A skyscraper's steel frame carries its own weight plus thousands of occupants.

punchline.text: Structures stand because engineers counted every force first.

quiz.question: What is the difference between dead loads and live loads?
options: Dead loads come from wind; live loads come from earthquakes
Dead loads are the building's own weight; live loads are movable forces
Dead loads act horizontally; live loads act vertically

details.summary: Structural loads are all the forces and pressures that a structure must resist throughout its life. Dead loads are permanent weight from the structure itself and fixed equipment. Live loads come from occupants, furniture, and movable objects.
details.whyItMatters: Accurately identifying and quantifying every load a structure will experience is the first and most critical step in structural design. Underestimating loads leads directly to structural failure.
takeaways: Dead loads are permanent forces from the structure's own weight and fixed elements
Live loads vary over time from occupants, vehicles, and movable equipment
Load combinations determine the most critical design scenario for each member

faq.question: Why do engineers consider multiple load combinations rather than just adding all loads together?
faq.answer: Not all loads occur simultaneously at maximum intensity. Wind and earthquake rarely happen together. Maximum live load on all floors simultaneously is statistically improbable. Load combination factors account for the probability of concurrent loading.

faq.question: How are live load values determined for building design?
faq.answer: Building codes specify minimum design live loads based on occupancy type derived from statistical surveys of actual usage. Office floors require 2.4 kPa, residential floors 1.9 kPa, and assembly areas 4.8 kPa.
